diagnosticTips: Passwords: Operate level, Config level and C7000AT menu are all '0000' at delivery (G57 2.1); no limit on attempts. Operate/Config passwords are stored per C7000IOC.
Reset: C7000AT RESET key once = mute, again = reset all alarms; C7000IOC command 'alarmreset' or 'ar'. All alarms except 'unreliable eev' need a manual reset.
Text spelling varies by software/variant: G57 'Low pressure 1', older 'LOW PRESSURE 1', EC Tower 'LOW PRE. 1 ERROR' - same alarm.
'Comp n Failure/HP' covers both the HP switch and the compressor internal power switch/MCB.
LP alarm is suppressed for the winter start delay (default 180 s) after compressor start; LP/HP alarm delay default 5 s.
On C7000IOC type 'state' to see alarms (passive display).
µPC (EC compressor) alarms are hidden for 240 s and auto-reset by the IOC a limited number of times per 24 h.
Unit stopped without alarm: check event log for Local Stop, Remote Stop, BMS stop 1/2, Timer Stop, Sequenc. Alarm Stop.
RTC failure (time wrong after power cycle) - IOC < 4.13 loses configuration; RTC part M24826.

Factory defaults (G57 ch. 11): setpoint 24 °C / 45 %rh; compressor pause 180 s, min runtime 180 s; LP/HP alarm delay 5 s; winter start delay 180 s; room limit alarms 5/35 °C (30 s delay); EEV superheat 7 K normal / 12 K dehumidification.

LP management (on/off compressors only) allows a number of restarts after LP trips before latching the alarm (epmintries 6, epmin 4.6 bar, epminint 2 h); HP management counts exceedances of cpmax (21 bar).

Zone valid-alarm numbers (Config Z3, used for standby changeover/BMS) differ from the MIB list: 01 Local stop, 04 E-heating, 05 Humidifier, 08 Fan error, 09 Filter, 13 Water detector, 24 Fire/smoke, 28 Phase failure, 30/31/32 Refrigerant circuit 1/2/1&2; default valid alarms 1-13, 24-27.
STULZ bus must be daisy-chained (not star). 'ADDRESS CONFLICT' shows only on the unit causing it and clears after re-addressing.
'#' in alarm texts stands for the component number; this pack lists the generic text plus numbered copies for 1-2 (heaters 1-3).
From 1 April 2024 new CyberAir 3PRO CW units ship with the STULZ GmbH E² touch controller, whose alarm list is NOT in this pack; do not apply C7000 or US E2 texts to it without the G50 manual.

diagnosticTips: Reset: press RESET once to silence the alarm tone, again to cancel the alarm.
Alarm inputs are fail-safe: +24 V = no alarm; loss of voltage (e.g. broken cable) = alarm.
D = adjustable delay 0-255 s; limit alarms 0-2550 s.
Fire and Water alarms are evaluated even with the unit stopped.
Air flow, compressor HP/LP, heater, humidifier and ultrasonic faults start the stand-by module.
If the return sensor fails during return-air control the display shows 32 °F and control changes to supply air.

I/O transmission failure: check Service > Equipment > Modules, the I/O board address switches and the cable per wiring diagram; if the fault continues from one module onward suspect the cable between the last good and first bad module, else replace the I/O board.

Stand-by module: false start (air flow, HP/LP, heater, humidifier, ultrasonic faults) has priority 1; alarm start begins 1.5 K / 3 %rh before the limit values. Sequencing rotates the stand-by module weekly.

controls.description: Carel pCO-based controller on STULZ USA (Frederick MD) units: graphic terminal, large-bezel terminal or touch screen (blue status = normal, red = alarm). Critical alarms shut the unit down until cleared and reset; Non-Critical alarms annunciate and drive the Summary Fault relay. Menus: Info/Alarm log (no password), Control (level 1, factory password 1), Service (level 2, factory password 2), Factory (level 3, per-controller password from STULZ Product Support via the Access ID Code), Configuration (level 4). Passwords changed in Service>Save Cfg. Not the same as the 2024 STULZ GmbH E² touch controller.
appliesTo: CyberRow (see stulz-e2-cyberrow for its own list)

diagnosticTips: Published factory passwords: Control menu = 1 (level 1), Service menu = 2 (level 2); changed in Service>Save Cfg. A higher-level password also opens lower menus. Factory menu password is per controller: give STULZ Product Support (888-529-1266) the Access ID Code shown on the Enter Password screen. Session times out after 300 s without key activity.
Reset: press the Alarm key to view, fix the cause, press Alarm again to clear. Critical alarms shut the unit down until cleared and reset. Hold Enter for 3 s to turn the unit off.

US DX pressure switches (R-410A; CyberRow DX, Mini-Space EC, CyberAir DX IOMs): HP opens at 630 psig, MANUAL reset; LP opens 65 psig (±10), closes 105 psig (±10), automatic reset - reset a tripped HP switch physically before the alarm will clear.
R-410A normal values (US IOMs): suction 130 psig (105-155), superheat 15 °F (10-20), subcooling 10 °F (5-20), condensing 125 °F at 95 °F ambient; fan cycling on at 440 psig.
Fan Failure on non-Modbus EC fans: most common cause is loose wires; E2 alarms on loss of 24 VAC at the fan alarm input.
Fire panel: External Fire Contact method needs manual reset and restart of every unit; Remote Power Off and Remote On/Off restart automatically (set EPO option = 1).
Status 'OFF - Manual Restart Req' = Automatic On disabled (Service>Options).
Factory defaults: 72 °F / 45 %RH; restore in Service>Save Cfg.
On EC fan failure remaining fans speed up; on Modbus loss fans keep last speed.
Controller 0-10 V fan signal must appear within 15 s of power-on or unit enters Air Proving Alarm.
CyberWall AHU uses the different E2 pluS BACnet controller (stulz-e2-plus-cyberwall), not this alarm list.
Work groups (pLAN, lead + up to 7): Active/Standby/Assist duties; a unit stopped by the group shows 'Off by Network'; rotation period typically 1 week.

ledPatterns.meaning: Alarm present or not yet reset; press Alarm key to view, again after fix to clear
pLAN / WinLoad status (Table 38 in OWR0129C; patterns shown as icons in the PDF)
checks: Compare with the table in the IOM PDF

diagnosticTips: Passwords (OWR0129C Table 22 / OWR0117E Table 13): Control 1, Service 2; Factory via STULZ Product Support (888-529-1266) with the Access ID Code.
Reset: press the Alarm key to view, fix the cause, press Alarm again to clear; 'System Fails to Start - Critical alarm condition not cleared. Press Alarm key to reset alarm'.

Custom Alarm relay = bitmask over 48 numbered alarms: 1 Upper fan, 2 Lower fan, 3 Middle fan, 4 Moisture, 5 Emergency shutdown, 6 Remote shutdown, 7 Customer alarm 1, 8 Airflow, 9 Filter, 10 Fire/smoke, 11 Water detection, 12 Condensate pan, 13 Circuit1 low pressure, 14 Circuit1 high pressure, 15/16 Dual power input A/B, 17 Humidifier, 18-21 High/Low temperature/humidity, 22/23 High/Low water temperature CW1, 24 Loss of power, 25-34 sensor failures, 41 System Off, 42 BMS keep alive off, 43/44 Customer alarm 2/3, 45 Flow switch. Factory totals 191/62/129/255/3/0.
Group alarms (Service>Group screen 6, all default 0) switch the unit to 'Off by internal alarm' and rotate in a standby unit.
HP switch 630 psig manual reset; LP switch 65/105 psig auto reset (R-410A).
Fan 0-10 VDC must be present within 15 s of power-on or the controller goes to Air Proving Alarm mode.
Temperature/humidity alarms are masked for 30 min after start-up.
BMS keep-alive (variable 100) must toggle 1/2 within 10 minutes or BMS-written live values revert.
Charge check (R-410A): superheat 15 °F (10-20), subcooling 10 °F (5-20), suction 130 psig (105-155); EEV superheat factory-set 12-15 °F by the EVD driver on the electric box door.
Condenser pressure too low on W/G units: 'Control pressure set too low. R-410A - Readjust to 440 psig.'

commonIssues.symptom: US E2 'Fan Failure' / 'Fan #n Failure' alarm on a non-Modbus EC fan
likelyCauses: Loose wires (most common cause per STULZ, not a defective motor)
Fan lost a phase, or high/low supply voltage (motor refuses to run)
Motor starter protector tripped or contactor contacts pitted
No 0-10 VDC speed signal (must appear within 15 s of power-on or the controller goes to Air Proving Alarm mode)
EC fan internal protection: blocked rotor, low supply or phase loss > 5 s (auto reset); electronics/motor over-temperature (reset by removing power for 20 s)
checks: Measure 24 VAC between the fan alarm input (ID8, ID11, ID12) and 24VAC-; no voltage = alarm
All 3 phases present and > 2.5 VDC on AIn1/GND (polarity sensitive; a 9 V battery can simulate the signal)
Do not judge the motor by winding continuity (internal AC/DC conversion)
Temporary jumper X2.A1 to the fan failure input keeps the contactor energized while testing - remove after
sources: STULZ 'Troubleshooting an EC Fan (Non Modbus) in a STULZ unit' (https://repository.stulz.com/016C2C75/)

commonIssues.symptom: High head pressure trip (E2 'High Head Pressure') on US DX units - alarm will not clear
likelyCauses: HP switch tripped at 630 psig - it is MANUAL reset
Condenser air intake blocked or coil dirty / condenser fan not running (air-cooled)
Low water/glycol flow, water/glycol too hot, valves partly closed, air in loop, glycol not premixed (W/G units)
Head pressure / water regulating valve set too high
checks: Reset the HP switch physically after fixing the cause, then reset the alarm at the display
Condenser fans and fan cycling/speed control (fan on 440 psig R-410A)
Subcooling 10 °F (5-20) and superheat 15 °F (10-20) with R-410A; for non-condensables recover, replace drier, evacuate to 50 microns, recharge
sources: STULZ CyberRow DX IOM OWR0129C, Table 46 and 3.13-3.15 (https://dam.stulz.com/pinaccess/showpin.do?pinCode=xQh6bxXY8bXK)
STULZ Mini-Space EC IOM OZU0001-B, Table 8 (https://repository.stulz.com/6894588C/STULZ_Mini-Space_IOM_OZU0001-B.pdf)

commonIssues.symptom: Low suction pressure (E2 'Low Suction Pressure') on US DX units
likelyCauses: Loss of refrigerant (bubbles in sight glass)
Low airflow: dirty filters or coil, obstructions, fan rotation
Expansion valve / EEV or electronic hot gas bypass (EVD driver) fault
checks: LP switch opens 65 psig (±10), closes 105 psig (±10), automatic reset
Suction pressure normal 130 psig (105-155) R-410A; superheat 10-20 °F
EVD driver status / alarms on the electric box door
sources: STULZ CyberRow DX IOM OWR0129C, Table 46 (https://dam.stulz.com/pinaccess/showpin.do?pinCode=xQh6bxXY8bXK)
STULZ CyberOne DX IOM OCC0096A troubleshooting (https://dam.stulz.com/pinaccess/showpin.do?pinCode=SGj4YZmttdbg)

commonIssues.symptom: C7000 'Comp n Failure/HP' (or 'COMP n ERROR/HP', 'Compressor # error')
likelyCauses: HP switch / HP threshold exceeded: condenser coil soiled, condenser fan defective, overcharge, HP setting too low, outside temperature too high
Compressor internal power switch (MCB / motor protector) tripped: motor defective or supply voltage too low under load
HP switch cable loose or defective
checks: Press the red release button on the HP switch after fixing, then RESET twice on the C7000AT
Compressor MCB, motor current and supply voltage under load
Condenser / drycooler operation and water flow
sources: STULZ CyberLab Original instructions G17F 02.2018, malfunction table (https://chiller-pro.ru/pdf/man/instr_Stulz_Cyberlab.pdf)

commonIssues.symptom: C7000 'Low pressure n' trips at start-up in cold weather
likelyCauses: Low condensing pressure at low ambient
Winter start delay set to 0 (LP alarm inhibit after compressor start, default 180 s)
checks: Winter start delay (default 180 s, command 'winterdelay 180') and LP alarm delay (default 5 s)
sources: STULZ C7000 G57 6.2019 ch. 11 defaults and sect. 5 (https://rafstjorn.is/wp-content/uploads/2019/11/STULZ_C7000R_G57_0619_en.pdf)

commonIssues.symptom: Unit is off but no alarm is shown
likelyCauses: C7000 event: Local Stop, Remote Stop, BMS stop 1/2, Timer Stop, Sequenc. Alarm Stop (standby rotation), Fire alarm stop
US E2 status: 'Off by Remote Shutdown', 'Off by Clock', 'Off by Network' (group/BMS), 'OFF - Manual Restart Req' (Automatic On disabled)
C6000/C5000: unit is the stand-by module
checks: Read the C7000AT event log or the E2 main-screen status line
Remote on/off contact (E2 X2.5-X2.6), BMS commands, week program / clock

commonIssues.symptom: Compressor will not start or short cycles (US DX)
likelyCauses: Setpoint too high / insufficient heat load
Internal overload open, LP switch open on loss of charge, HP switch tripped
Dirty or iced coil, reduced airflow
Supply/return grilles too close or remote sensor badly located
checks: Airflow and coil condition; scroll compressor noisy = phase at the main supply, do not rewire the compressor
sources: STULZ CyberOne DX IOM OCC0096A troubleshooting (https://dam.stulz.com/pinaccess/showpin.do?pinCode=SGj4YZmttdbg)
STULZ Mini-Space EC IOM OZU0001-B, Table 8 (https://repository.stulz.com/6894588C/STULZ_Mini-Space_IOM_OZU0001-B.pdf)

likelyCauses: Discharge air short-cycling back to return
sources: STULZ Mini-Space EC IOM OZU0001-B, Table 8 (https://repository.stulz.com/6894588C/STULZ_Mini-Space_IOM_OZU0001-B.pdf)

commonIssues.symptom: Steam humidifier inoperative or E2 'Humidifier' alarm
likelyCauses: Humidifier breaker tripped (over-current at the electrodes)
Water conductivity too low (usually first start-up)
Cylinder at end of life (yellow LED flashes four times repeatedly)
checks: Breaker: drain the cylinder and refill, then reset
Low conductivity: add about 1/4 teaspoon (1.23 ml) of table salt through the top of the cylinder
Yellow LED flashing: consult the humidifier manual; replace the cylinder if 4 flashes
sources: STULZ Mini-Space EC IOM OZU0001-B, Table 8 (https://repository.stulz.com/6894588C/STULZ_Mini-Space_IOM_OZU0001-B.pdf)

commonIssues.symptom: Chilled-water unit short of capacity or CW valve does not open/close
likelyCauses: Low CW flow (blocked lines, clogged strainer, valves partly closed)
No control power to the valve actuator or actuator failed
checks: CW supply/return temperatures and flow (E2 'True No Flow' / 'No Flow Water Temp')
0-10 V valve signal and actuator supply

commonIssues.symptom: Locked out of the E2 Control / Service / Factory menus
likelyCauses: Session timed out (300 s without key activity)
Factory level needs a controller-specific password
checks: Try the published factory passwords: Control = 1, Service = 2
Factory menu: call STULZ Product Support 888-529-1266 with the Access ID Code shown on the Enter Password screen
CyberWall E2 pluS: display password 318; web UI admin / Stulzadmin1
sources: STULZ CyberRow DX IOM OWR0129C Table 22 (https://dam.stulz.com/pinaccess/showpin.do?pinCode=xQh6bxXY8bXK)

commonIssues.symptom: Units stay off after a fire-alarm test
likelyCauses: E2 fire-panel method 1 (External Fire Contact X2.7-X2.8) needs each unit's Smoke Alarm reset and a manual restart
C7000 'Fire alarm stop' until alarm reset and local start
checks: Reset the alarm and turn each unit on at the display or via BMS
Methods 2 (Remote Power Off X2.3-X2.4) and 3 (Remote On/Off X2.5-X2.6, EPO option = 1) restart automatically
sources: STULZ 'Fire Panel Interface to the Stulz E2 Controller' (https://repository.stulz.com/FFDDB7DB/)

commonIssues.symptom: CyberWall runs although the BMS turned it off (fans at preset or max speed)
likelyCauses: BMS keep-alive point not updated within the keep-alive time (default 120 s) - BV34 BMS Keep Alive Al
checks: BMS must write the keep-alive point (AV30) every 120 s when it writes fan speed
Check AV31/AV32 keep-alive delays and the BMS integration

commonIssues.symptom: C7000 'BUS ERROR' / 'ADDRESS CONFLICT' or configuration lost after a power cycle
likelyCauses: Bus cable/termination or a unit powered off
Two units with the same bus address (shown only on the unit causing it; IOC error LED flashes)
STULZ bus wired as a star instead of a daisy chain
Real-time clock failure: time wrong after power cycle; IOC software older than 4.13 loses configuration
checks: Re-address the unit causing the conflict
Replace RTC (part M24826), set time/date, re-check bus address and BMS settings

commonIssues.symptom: Ultrasonic humidifier (DAH/DRH) produces no or too little mist
likelyCauses: Level Controller alarm - read the LED blink count (1 Low Voltage, 2 High Voltage, 3 Freeze, 4 High Temperature, 5 Low Water, 6 Fill Alarm, 7 Communications, 8 Transducer)
Water supply valve closed, float switch FS1 sticking, fill solenoid faulty
Supply voltage low (too little mist) or high (coarse mist)
Scale on transducers or dust in tank
checks: Remove the Mist Guide Cover and electrical access cover to see the LED
24 VDC at X2-1/X2-2 with the tank drained (fill solenoid)
Float switch continuity at terminal X3
Adjust the 48 VDC power supply output
sources: STULZ DRH Series Gen 2 IOM OUD0134 (https://dam.stulz.com/pinaccess/showpin.do?pinCode=bjJBak60ddxc)

commonIssues.symptom: Superheat reading wrong / EVD EEV alarms (LowSH, LOP, MOP, probe, motor)
likelyCauses: Pressure or temperature probe faulty or badly positioned
Wrong pressure probe type or refrigerant selected in the driver
Communication loss to the C7000/E2 (driver falls back to DI control)
checks: Probe readings vs gauges and thermometer
Power-cycle the driver after an EEV motor error to realign the valve
Factory superheat: C7000 7 K / 12 K dehum; US CyberRow 12-15 °F

likelyCauses: Loss of refrigerant (bubbles in sight glass)
Condenser fan controls not set correctly
W/G units: control pressure set too low
checks: Water/glycol head pressure valve: readjust to 440 psig (R-410A) / 320 psig (R407C)
sources: STULZ CyberRow DX IOM OWR0129C, Table 46 (https://dam.stulz.com/pinaccess/showpin.do?pinCode=xQh6bxXY8bXK)

notes: Two separate code systems: STULZ GmbH (Hamburg) type codes with spaces (ASR 291 A, CCD 111 A, CRS 251 GES, ESO 7402 AHF) and STULZ USA / Air Technology Systems (Frederick, MD) hyphenated codes (CFD-105-D2W-0-I0, CRS-090-C, CCD-121-W-EC, COS-042-G-FC-U-EC, OHS-040-HG-FC). US capacity is kW on CF and CC codes but MBH on COS, VFS, OHS and CRS.

Serial numbers: no date decode is published. STULZ GmbH rating plates (in the door in front of the electrical compartment) print the year of manufacture directly next to the serial number, so read the year from the plate. STULZ USA nameplates (inside the cabinet / electrical box; CeilAir: outside near the electric box) show model, serial, STULZ item/job number, refrigerant, FLA/MCA/MOP - no year code is documented; use the wiring-diagram date or ask STULZ USA support (888-529-1266) with the serial and item number.

Controllers: C5000/C6000 (legacy), C7000 (GmbH ~2004-2024), STULZ GmbH E² touch controller (2024+, first on CyberAir 3PRO CW - alarm list not obtained, so no platform is included for it), US E2 Series (Carel pCO-based) on all Frederick-built units, E2 pluS on CyberWall, Ultra-Series on ultrasonic humidifier systems. Do not confuse the US E2 with the GmbH E².

Fault-code entries for C7000 alarms that contain '#' (component number) are listed both generically and as numbered copies (1-2, heaters 1-3) so the displayed text matches; EC Tower, CyberLab and older 10.06 spellings that read differently are separate entries.
A-Tech-20 alarms are listed by their Carel Modbus gateway point description (Modbus address in the meaning) rather than by register number.

Not covered: GmbH E² (2024+) alarm list, CyberAir Mini / CyberCool 2 / CyberHandler 2 controller alarm lists, Carel humiSteam / SupraSteam humidifier codes, ebm-papst fan-side LED codes, GPS pump-package and drycooler nomenclature (published only as images).
